questions.question: A family drives from a Virginia county, through a town with its own council, and into a city that elects its own council and runs its own schools separately from any county. Which three kinds of local government has the family passed through?
questions.correctAnswer: A county, a town, and an independent city
distractors: A parish, a borough, and a township
A province, a prefecture, and a district
A reservation, a territory, and a commonwealth district
questions.explanation: Virginia local government is built from counties, cities and towns. Towns sit inside counties and share some services with them, while Virginia cities are independent of counties - a structure students meet again in the local-government standards.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Counties, towns and independent cities - Virginia's local trio.

questions.question: A family moves from a Virginia county into a nearby Virginia city and is surprised that the city is not part of any county at all - it has its own courts, school board and tax base, separate from the surrounding county. Which Virginia feature explains this?
questions.correctAnswer: Virginia's independent cities - cities are separate from counties and provide their own full range of local services
distractors: Home rule charters that remove cities from the Commonwealth
Federal city status granted to all Virginia cities in 1871
County annexation law that dissolves counties around cities
questions.explanation: Virginia is famous for independent cities: by law, a Virginia city is a separate jurisdiction, not part of any county, and it performs both city and county-level functions. Towns, by contrast, remain part of their counties.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A Virginia city stands alone - no county wrapped around it.

questions.question: A Virginia town council wants to create a new kind of local tax that no state law mentions, and the town attorney warns the council that it lacks the power. Which rule is the attorney applying?
questions.correctAnswer: The Dillon Rule - local governments have only the powers granted to them by the state
distractors: The Supremacy Clause - federal law must grant the tax first
The Tenth Amendment - towns hold all undelegated powers
Judicial review - only courts may create local taxes
questions.explanation: Under the Dillon Rule, named for a nineteenth-century judge, local governments are creatures of the state: they possess only powers expressly granted by the state, necessarily implied, or essential to their purposes. Virginia follows this rule strictly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Towns may do what Richmond allows - the Dillon Rule keeps the list.

questions.question: In one Virginia county, an elected board of supervisors sets the property tax and county budget, an elected school board runs the schools, and a sheriff and treasurer are elected separately. What does this structure show about Virginia local government?
questions.correctAnswer: Virginia local offices are often separately elected, dividing local power among boards and constitutional officers rather than one mayor-like executive
distractors: Virginia counties are run entirely by officials appointed in Richmond
Virginia local governments have no elected officials at all
Virginia towns and counties are governed directly by the governor
questions.explanation: Counties are governed by elected boards of supervisors, school governance sits with school boards, and voters separately elect constitutional officers such as the sheriff, treasurer and commonwealth's attorney. Cities use elected councils, often with an appointed manager.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Local power in Virginia is spread across many elected desks.

questions.question: A 19-year-old who was born in another state, moved to Virginia last year and lives in Norfolk wants to register to vote in Virginia. Which set of qualifications must she meet to register in the Commonwealth?
questions.correctAnswer: Be a US citizen, a resident of Virginia, and at least 18 years old by the general election, and not disqualified by a felony conviction or court finding
distractors: Be born in Virginia, own property in Norfolk, and be at least 21
Be employed by the Commonwealth and registered with a political party
Have lived in Virginia for five years and pass a civics examination
questions.explanation: Virginia registration follows the constitutional basics: citizenship, Virginia residency, and age 18 by election day. A felony conviction removes the right until the governor restores it, and a court finding of mental incapacity can also disqualify.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Citizen, Virginian, eighteen - the registration checklist starts there.

questions.question: A new Virginia resident registers while renewing a license at the DMV, her roommate registers online, and their neighbor mails a paper form to the local registrar - all before the registration deadline. What does their experience show about voting in Virginia under CE.10b?
questions.correctAnswer: Virginia offers several registration routes - online, by mail, in person and at the DMV - with a regular deadline before the election and same-day registration with a provisional ballot afterward
distractors: Virginia registers voters automatically at birth with no action needed
Only in-person registration at the Capitol is valid in Virginia
Registration in Virginia closes a full year before each election
questions.explanation: CE.10b covers how Virginians register and vote: applications are accepted online, by mail, at registrars' offices and through agencies such as the DMV. Registering by the regular deadline lets a voter cast a regular ballot; since 2022, a voter who misses that deadline may still register in person up to and including Election Day and vote a provisional ballot.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Many doors into the voter rolls - miss the regular deadline and same-day registration with a provisional ballot remains.

questions.question: Virginia voters in a single election choose a governor, a lieutenant governor and an attorney general on separate ballot lines, and the winners sometimes come from different parties. Which feature of Virginia's executive branch does this reveal?
questions.correctAnswer: Virginia elects its top three executive officers separately, so executive power at the top is shared rather than chosen as one ticket
distractors: Virginia's governor appoints the other two officers after the election
The three officers are chosen by the General Assembly, not voters
Federal law requires every state to elect three executives separately
questions.explanation: Article V structures a plural executive at the top: the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general are each elected statewide in their own races. The arrangement can divide the Commonwealth's executive leadership between parties.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Three separate races, three separate winners - Virginia splits its top jobs.

Dulles Airport, which handles all Virginia cargo by sea
The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, Virginia's main modern freight route

Virginia is largely cut off from the national economy by its independent cities
Federal spending plays no measurable role in Virginia's economy
questions.explanation: CE.12g places Virginia inside the US and global economies. questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Federal jobs, ships, servers and farms - Virginia runs on four engines.

questions.correctAnswer: Local governments lean most on the property (real estate) tax; together the bills show that each level of government raises its own revenue for its own budget
distractors: The federal government leans most on property tax; the bills show one shared budget
Counties lean most on income tax; the bills show states collect all revenue
Cities lean most on tariffs; the bills show trade taxes fund local schools
questions.explanation: CE.13c compares budgets and taxes at the three levels. Virginia localities fund schools, police and services chiefly through real-estate property taxes, while the Commonwealth relies mainly on income and sales taxes and the federal government on income and payroll taxes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Property tax feeds the county; income tax feeds Richmond and Washington.

questions.question: Virginia's governor unveils a spending plan covering two fiscal years, the General Assembly amends and passes it, and agencies then spend under it while the next plan is drafted. Which budget feature of Virginia government is on display?
questions.correctAnswer: Virginia budgets on a two-year (biennial) cycle, proposed by the governor and enacted by the General Assembly
distractors: Virginia budgets monthly, proposed by county boards and enacted by courts
Virginia has no budget process because taxes are voluntary
Virginia's budget is written by Congress as part of the federal budget
questions.explanation: Virginia operates on a biennial budget: the governor proposes a two-year spending plan and the General Assembly debates, amends and enacts it, with the governor able to sign or use the line-item veto on budget items. CE.13c covers this state budget process alongside local and federal ones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two years at a time - the governor proposes, the Assembly disposes.
